title: The wedding in the code
hookLine: the four lavan, no dowry, no child marriage

cards: No exchange of rings at the center of it. No vows written by the couple. No officiant asking if anyone objects.
At a Sikh wedding the couple sits side by side on the floor before the Guru Granth Sahib, the groom's scarf in the bride's hand, linking them. A hymn is read.

Then it's sung, and as it's sung the couple rises and walks slowly around the Granth, the groom ahead, the bride following, the cloth between them. They sit. Another verse is read, and they walk again.
By the end they have circled the Guru, and they're married.

teach.h: ANAND KARAJ: THE CEREMONY OF BLISS.
teach.b: Anand Karaj means the ceremony of bliss. Anand is bliss, the same word as the Anand Sahib we heard at the bhog, and karaj is a ceremony or an undertaking.

teach.h: THE LAVAN, A HYMN IN FOUR ROUNDS.
teach.b: The heart of it is the lavan, a hymn by Guru Ram Das on Ang seven hundred seventy-three of the Guru Granth Sahib, in four stanzas.
Each stanza is one lav, one round, read and then sung while the couple walks around the Granth.

teach.h: A JOURNEY OF THE SOUL TO GOD.
teach.b: In paraphrase, the rounds move like a journey: the first is about taking up a life of duty and remembering the Name; the second about losing fear and meeting the Lord in every place; the third about longing and love in the company of the holy; the fourth about peace, the union found.

Read that way, the hymn is about the soul and God, and the couple is invited to see their marriage inside that larger love. Now the code. The Sikh Rehat Maryada surrounds the ceremony with rules that protect people.

teach.h: NO CASTE, NO DOWRY, NO CHILD BRIDE.
teach.b: In paraphrase: a marriage should be arranged without regard to caste. No child marriage. No dowry.
No consulting the stars for a lucky date or hour. Each removes a way a wedding can become a transaction or a burden, especially for a young bride and her family.
What's left is simple: two people, the Guru, a hymn and four rounds.

how: At a Sikh wedding the couple sits before the Guru Granth Sahib; each of the four lavan of Guru Ram Das is read and then sung while the couple walks around the Granth, and Ardas and karah prashad follow.

o: the Sikh wedding, four rounds around the Guru Granth Sahib
a feast of thanks held after a full reading of the Granth
the joyful hymn sung at the close of every service

games.q: two families want a Sikh wedding but argue about caste and a dowry. what does the code say?
o: no regard to caste, and no dowry.
both are up to the families.
games.why: the code says marriage should be without regard to caste, and rules out dowry and child marriage.

practice: Bring to mind two people who share a life, newlyweds, your parents, friends who've come through a hard year, and picture them walking slowly together, one step behind the other, the way a couple walks the rounds.
Hold them there and wish them steadiness, kindness and peace between them; if you pray, hold them before Waheguru.
